findings.title: [P3] Confirm `release()` cannot throw or reject — it would replace the work outcome
findings.body: Deterministic JS semantics: a synchronous throw inside `finally` replaces the try block's pending completion. If the external `release()` callback ever throws, a successful `work()` result is discarded and `withLock` rejects with the release error, and an original `work()` rejection would be masked by it; if `release()` instead returns a rejected promise, it is unhandled. The `locks` contract is defined nowhere in this repo, so the trigger is unconfirmed — hence a confirm-intended note rather than a defect. Relative to the base branch (which never released at all) this change is a strict improvement. If the external contract allows release failures, consider guarding or awaiting the call.
